data.note:
Missed actin-disruptor call: I over-weighted bright compact tubulin/actin masses and rising tub_mean as stabilizer-specific, when rounding/shrinkage concentrates signal in both Eg5 and stabilizer phenotypes as the reviewer warned. Two microscopist reads favoring stabilizer outweighed a weak NSC Eg5 vote (sim ~0.55), and actin-disruptor was never on the board despite huge act_std/contrast signals.

Literature now clarifies the true mechanism: cytochalasin D caps actin filaments to block polymerization (PMID:3023337) with structural capping/severing activity (PMID:40658853), which can collapse cells into bright rounded masses that mimic mitotic arrest in low-resolution DAPI/tubulin/actin images.

Fix: keep actin-disruptors alive when actin texture explodes even if tubulin also rises, and require high-resolution spindle/actin-aggregate scoring to separate bundling vs monopolar vs actin clumps.

reflection.text:
We correctly detected a potent, dose-dependent cytoskeletal antimitotic phenotype: extreme act_std z=+139.0 to +179.3 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+138.7 to +185.2 at 1-10 uM, falling but still strong at 0.1-0.3 uM, with monotonic rises in frac_mitotic_like and tub_mean and lower density. That justified an antimitotic hypothesis and the Eg5 vs stabilizer uncertainty we tracked.

We were wrong because Actin disruptors were never in the hypothesis set, so the strongest clue — actin texture as the top feature — was reframed as microtubule biology. We over-weighted NSC 3/4 Eg5 votes at modest similarities 0.56-0.60 and k-neighbours split Eg5/destabilizer, and we over-read tub_mean rho=+1.00 as stabilizer mass increase when rounding/shrinkage from actin collapse concentrates signal, as the review warned. Two microscopist calls favoring Microtubule stabilizers from saturated 10 uM fields and then 0.3 uM bright masses sealed the error, mistaking condensed microtubules for bundled stabilizer microtubules.

In hindsight the acquisition order hurt us: starting at 1 and 10 uM saturated spindle polarity, and the first conclusion preceded the requested 0.3 uM interphase description. Cytochalasin D capping/severing of actin (PMID 3023337, PMID 40658853) and monomer binding (PMID 3782101) explains both the dominant actin scores and the secondary mitotic-like, tubulin-bright morphology that mimicked Eg5/stabilizer arrest.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: Eg5 inhibitors 0.45, Microtubule stabilizers 0.25, Microtubule destabilizers 0.20, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.10
- after step 12: Eg5 inhibitors 0.55, Microtubule stabilizers 0.25, Microtubule destabilizers 0.13, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.07
- after step 15: Microtubule stabilizers 0.60, Eg5 inhibitors 0.25, Microtubule destabilizers 0.10, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.05

## Conclusion 1

**Eg5 inhibitors** (stated probability 0.55); key evidence e9, e2, e3, e11, e10.

Why: NSC 3/4 votes leading class with monotonic mitotic arrest; single microscopist view favors stabilizer but notes Eg5 cannot be excluded.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: High-resolution tubulin plus centrosome staining to score monopolar rosette spindles versus bipolar/bundled spindles, with reference treatments of the Eg5 and stabilizer classes as comparators.

## Conclusion 2

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.60); key evidence e14, e4, e10, e9, e11.

Why: Two doses microscopist favors stabilizer with loss of radial network to bright masses; tub mass rises monotonically; NSC Eg5 similarities modest.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: High-resolution tubulin plus centrosome staining to score bundled interphase microtubules and bipolar versus monopolar spindles, with reference treatments of the stabilizer and Eg5 classes as comparators.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Top call rests mainly on the NSC 3/4 Eg5 vote and a monotonic rise in mitotic fraction and tubulin mean, neither of which separates Eg5 inhibition from microtubule stabilisation: both cause mitotic rounding/shrinkage that concentrates signal and inflates mean intensity. The only direct microscopy assessment (saturated 10 µM fields) actually favoured stabilisers, noted spindle polarity could not be resolved, and tubulin-mass increase was cited for stabilisers. Microscopy was never repeated at the lower, less saturated doses the agent acquired precisely to discriminate these classes, so the 0.55 probability is not yet calibrated to the evidence.

Requested: FREE ANALYSIS: run phenotype description on the already-acquired 0.3 µM well (dose index 4, replicate 1, w_b617e84d8d; no new acquisition). Score predominantly non-mitotic interphase cells for bundled bright microtubules (stabiliser) versus an intact radial network (Eg5), and describe any mitotic spindle configuration present.

## Unblinding

Compound: **cytochalasin D** (PubChem CID [5458428](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5458428))

Identity check: name only (the BBBC021 structure is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

## Reflection

We correctly detected a potent, dose-dependent cytoskeletal antimitotic phenotype: extreme act_std z=+139.0 to +179.3 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+138.7 to +185.2 at 1-10 uM, falling but still strong at 0.1-0.3 uM, with monotonic rises in frac_mitotic_like and tub_mean and lower density. That justified an antimitotic hypothesis and the Eg5 vs stabilizer uncertainty we tracked.

We were wrong because Actin disruptors were never in the hypothesis set, so the strongest clue — actin texture as the top feature — was reframed as microtubule biology. We over-weighted NSC 3/4 Eg5 votes at modest similarities 0.56-0.60 and k-neighbours split Eg5/destabilizer, and we over-read tub_mean rho=+1.00 as stabilizer mass increase when rounding/shrinkage from actin collapse concentrates signal, as the review warned. Two microscopist calls favoring Microtubule stabilizers from saturated 10 uM fields and then 0.3 uM bright masses sealed the error, mistaking condensed microtubules for bundled stabilizer microtubules.

In hindsight the acquisition order hurt us: starting at 1 and 10 uM saturated spindle polarity, and the first conclusion preceded the requested 0.3 uM interphase description. Cytochalasin D capping/severing of actin (PMID 3023337, PMID 40658853) and monomer binding (PMID 3782101) explains both the dominant actin scores and the secondary mitotic-like, tubulin-bright morphology that mimicked Eg5/stabilizer arrest.

What was right:
- Detected strong dose-dependent cytoskeletal disruption with extreme actin and tubulin texture z-scores and rising frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00
- Flagged Eg5 vs microtubule stabilizer ambiguity and that 10 uM fields were saturated with unresolved spindle polarity
- Acquired lower doses 0.1 and 0.3 uM to test onset and sought second phenotype description per review

What was wrong or missed:
- Excluded Actin disruptors from all hypothesis updates despite act_std and act_glcm_contrast as top features at e2, e3, e8
- Over-weighted NSC Eg5 3/4 vote with low similarities 0.559-0.599 while ignoring split k-neighbours and no actin comparison
- Misinterpreted monotonic tub_mean increase as stabilizer-specific rather than secondary condensation from actin-driven rounding
- Accepted microscopist stabilizer calls based on loss of radial network to bright masses without actin-channel discrimination at non-saturated interphase cells

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution paired phalloidin-actin plus tubulin imaging at 0.1-0.3 uM with cytochalasin D / latrunculin reference controls to score actin clumps, loss of stress fibers, multinucleation and secondary microtubule condensation versus true bundling or monopolar spindles.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [3023337](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3023337/): Actin polymerization. The mechanism of action of cytochalasin D. *J Biol Chem* (1986) — Cytochalasin D inhibits actin polymerization by capping filament barbed ends.
- PMID [40658853](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40658853/): Microscopic and structural observations of actin filament capping and severing by cytochalasin D. *Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A* (2025) — Structural and microscopic work shows cytochalasin D caps and severs actin filaments.
- PMID [3782101](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3782101/): The kinetics of cytochalasin D binding to monomeric actin. *J Biol Chem* (1986) — Cytochalasin D binds monomeric actin with defined kinetics.
